title: Trapping e/4 quasiparticles in bilayer graphene
why_careful: Calibration of the antidot-gate method on known states (ν = −1, −4/3) against top-gate data, magnetic-field periods alongside gate periods, repeated-sweep histograms where the gate is unstable, null doubling at odd-denominator states up to the maximum side-gate voltage, bulk incompressibility monitored during every sweep, and a temperature-dependence regime test.

spans: Since these two states have already been characterized in
detail using the TG [30], we use them here to calibrate
the ADG oscillations and verify the analysis procedure,
see the Supp. Material for the characterization using
the TG. From the two-dimensional fast Fourier trans-
form (2D-FFT) in Fig. 1g–h, we find that the ratio be-
tween the ADG voltage period at ν = −4/3 and that
at ν = −1 is equal to ∆V /∆V1 = 0.37 ± 0.04, in agree-
ment with the value q/e = 1/3 expected for CD antidot
oscillations previously reported. The ratio between the
magnetic field period at ν = −1 and that at ν = −4/3 is
equal to ∆B1 /∆B = 3.47 ± 0.79, consistent with the ex-
pected p = 4 quasiparticles per flux quantum, within the
uncertainty.
We therefore conclude that the ADG provides reliable
local control of the AD and that our analysis reproduces
the previously benchmarked behaviour in a similar de-
vice [30].

If electrons tunnel at ν = −1 and quasiparticles with charge e/3 tunnel at ν = −4/3, the corresponding top-gate
periodicities are expected to differ by a factor of three, such that ∆Vtg (ν = −1)/∆Vtg (ν = −4/3) = 3. When using
the periods extracted from the 2D-FFT, find ∆Vtg (ν = −1)/∆Vtg (ν = −4/3) = 2.9±0.6, consistent with the expected

ratio. This is the same principle used in our previous related work, where the quasiparticle charge was inferred using
only the top-gate periodicity [30].
info.why: the benchmark on ν = −1 and −4/3 is what shows the antidot-gate periods follow Coulomb-dominated charge addition before the ratios are read as charge

spans: This data set shows substantial
gate instability, therefore we validate the periodicity with
a second, independent method following Ref. [34]: we
build a histogram of the oscillations by repeatedly ac-
quiring the same trace, and repeat the procedure at sev-
eral magnetic fields. Tracking the shift of the dominant
histogram peak with magnetic field gives an estimate of
∆B that agrees with the value extracted from the 2D-
FFT (see Supp. Material).
Also in this case, the period values obtained
at ν = 2/3 have been cross-checked with the histogram
method reported in the Supp. Material.

This procedure yields a magnetic-field periodicity consistent with
the value obtained from the 2D-FFT.
info.why: the repeated-sweep histogram check is the only answer to the gate instability seen at ν = 2/3

spans: However, the
absence of doubling in the conventional odd-denominator
states studied here suggests that the effect is linked to
the specific edge-structure of the underlying state, rather
than being an inherent feature of the device geometry.
, whereas no doubling is found at
the odd-denominator FQH states ν = −4/3 and −1/3
(see Supp. Material).

In all three side-gate configurations, we
extract a charge consistent with e/3 and a magnetic-field periodicity corresponding to ϕ0 /4 (p = 4). No transition to the
Aharonov–Bohm regime is observed, or doubling of the gate voltage period, even at the maximum side-gate voltage of 5 V
allowed by the safe limits of the device.
info.why: the null result at odd-denominator states is the control showing period doubling is absent where it is not expected
